title: The Three Questions
summary: A powerful man asks three hard questions and visits a wise old person for help.
coverScene: A wise old hermit digs his garden in the green hills while a thoughtful king watches quietly.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a powerful king wanted to know three important things.
He wanted to know the right time to begin each action.
He wanted to know who the most important people were.
He wanted to know what the most important task was.
Because no one could give him a good answer, he decided to visit an old man.
The old man lived in a garden near the forest.
Many people came to see him for advice.
The king dressed in plain clothes and walked alone until he reached the garden.
When the king asked his questions, the old man kept working without speaking.
Seeing that the old man was tired, the king took the tool and continued working.
Hours passed while the king worked, and the sun began to go down.
Suddenly, a bad stranger came out of the woods with a hurt arm.
The man was losing blood fast.
The king rushed over, cleaned the wound, and covered it carefully.
Tired from the hard labor, the king fell into bed on the floor.
When he woke up, the stranger looked at him with deep sadness.
The man explained that he was an enemy who had come to kill the king.
The king was glad to make peace and promised to give back all lands.
Before leaving, the king asked the old man one final time for the answers.
The old man explained that the most important time is now.
The person you are with is the most important person.
The good thing to do is to help that person.
The king thought about these words for a long time.
He understood that life is short and very valuable.
Every day brings new chances to do good things for others.
The king had learned a great lesson from the old man.
He walked back to his big house with a calm mind.
His heart was full of love for all people.
From that day on, the king tried to live a better life.
He always made sure to help anyone in need.
If a problem came up, he stayed calm and thought carefully.
He never forgot the important lesson he learned in the garden.
The country grew strong and calm under his rule.
People from far away came to hear his wonderful stories.
They wanted to know how he became such a good leader.
The king always told them about the old man in the garden.
He told them that the present moment is all we really have.
We must use our time well and always be kind to others.
This is the secret to a happy and good life.
Many years passed after that special day in the garden.
The king ruled his land with great care and constant attention.
If anyone had a serious problem, the king listened to them directly.
He walked among the citizens to see their daily lives.
Children played in the streets while adults worked in shops.
No one suffered from hunger because the king shared food freely.
The army stayed strong, but peace remained the main goal.
Visitors from foreign countries arrived to study the system.
They could not believe how well the community operated.
The king always shared his personal story with the guests.
He told every new generation about the wise old man.
The future depends on what we do right now.
Therefore, the king kept his heart open to every person.
He ensured that kindness guided every single action he took.
His name became a symbol of hope and proper leadership.
Even when difficult challenges appeared, he remained completely steady.
The country thrived and remained secure through all seasons.
Every single citizen felt safe and deeply respected.
The king smiled as he watched his people live well.
He knew that helping others brought true satisfaction.
His final years were filled with quiet strength and dignity.
When the king finally passed away, the whole nation mourned.
They remembered his fair laws and his gentle nature.
Statues were built to honor his memory in the capital.
Children learned about his wonderful rule in school.
The lesson of the garden lived on through the years.
People understood that the present moment is truly everything.
If we treat each other well, the world improves.
This simple truth remained the greatest guide for everyone.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a powerful king became entirely convinced that he would never fail if he knew three vital things.
He wanted to know the exact right time to begin each action, and who the most important people truly were.
Furthermore, he desperately wanted to discover what the most important task was in any given moment.
Because no one at court could give him a satisfactory answer, he decided to visit a wise old person.
This reclusive hermit lived simply in the hills, far away from the noise and flattery of the royal palace.
The wise person was widely known across the kingdom as a man who truly understood the fundamental nature of the world.
Determined to remain unrecognized, the king dressed himself in plain clothes and left his royal horse far behind.
He walked alone through winding mountain paths until he finally reached the small garden where the wise man worked every single day.
When the monarch arrived and asked his three pressing questions, the old man listened with profound and patient attention.
However, the hermit kept digging the dark earth without speaking a single word in response to the ruler.
Noticing that the old person was visibly frail and exhausted, the king decided to intervene out of genuine concern.
He gently stepped forward and took the heavy iron tool from the trembling hands of the hermit.
The king continued working in the garden for a long time, turning the stubborn soil under the increasingly warm sun.
Hours passed slowly while the royal visitor dug the earth, sweat pouring down his forehead in the late afternoon heat.
Soon the sun began to sink slowly behind the green hills as evening approached with a cool breeze.
Suddenly, a severely wounded and exhausted stranger burst out of the dense surrounding woods with a desperate cry.
The fugitive was holding his heavily injured arm tightly with both hands while dark blood ran down his sleeve.
Without a moment of hesitation, the king rushed over to the fallen man and knelt in the dirt beside him.
The compassionate ruler quickly cleaned the jagged wound and wrapped it carefully with clean linen material from his own tunic.
Then, with the help of the hermit, the king supported the injured person and led him inside the small room to rest.
Exhausted from the heavy physical labor and the emotional strain of the long day, the king collapsed on the wooden floor.
He fell into a deep and dreamless sleep right there on the hard floor of the simple house until the morning light arrived.
When he finally woke up the next morning, the stranger was staring straight at him with deep sorrow and tears shining in his eyes.
The recovering man asked for immediate pardon, deciding to confess his true identity and dark intentions to the surprised ruler.
He explained that he was a sworn enemy who had vowed to kill the king during this very journey across the mountains.
The assassin revealed that he had waited all day in the woods, expecting the king to return alone along the open path.
When the hours passed and the king failed to appear, the desperate man had left his hiding place to search for him.
Instead of finding an easy target, he had stumbled into the royal guards who recognized his face and wounded him severely.
However, despite knowing nothing about his identity, the king had saved his life with incredible care and generous medical support.
The astonished king was very glad to make complete peace with his former enemy, realizing the strange turn of fate.
Showing immense grace, the king promised to give back all the lands and properties that had been confiscated from the man's family.
He sent his guards away and treated the former conspirator not as a prisoner, but as a valued and honored guest.
Before leaving the small room to begin his journey home, the king asked the wise man one final time for the answers to his questions.
The wise old man looked up calmly and explained that the most important time in the world is always the present moment, which is now.
He stated clearly that the most important person is invariably the one you are actually with at that precise moment.
Finally, the wise hermit told the king that the most important task of all is simply to do that person good.
The king listened carefully to these simple words and understood their profound and lasting meaning in his soul.
He knew that his difficult journey had been completely successful because he had learned the most valuable lessons about human existence.
The ruler returned to his grand house with a remarkably calm mind and a clear, unburdened heart.
He spent the rest of his remaining days helping vulnerable people and doing good things for everyone across his entire country.
Whenever a difficult problem or political conflict came up, the king remembered the wise man words and paused to reflect.
He always focused intently on the present moment and the specific person standing right in front of him.
Peace and genuine happiness stayed in the land for many long and prosperous years under his thoughtful guidance.
The inspiring story of the king and the wise man was told from generation to generation across the whole nation with great admiration.
Simple citizens quickly learned that doing good for others is always the single right path to follow in life.
These simple lessons changed the heart of the powerful ruler forever, erasing his old arrogance and thirst for endless conquest.
He never forgot the three important things that he had discovered through hard experience away from his palace.
The king often walked through the palace gardens again, remembering the events of those transformative days in the hills.
He felt that his mind was remarkably clear and that his kingdom's future was brighter than it had ever been before.
Every single person in the country began to respect the wise ruler much more deeply than they had in the past.
The king shared his incredible story with his closest friends and family members during quiet evening gatherings.
They all agreed unanimously that helping others selflessly was the greatest purpose a human being could ever hope to have.
Life in the country became wonderfully peaceful and happy for all citizens, rich and poor alike.
The king continued to rule with extraordinary wisdom and complete fairness until the very end of his days on earth.
No more enemies ever came to trouble his peaceful lands, because kindness had built a wall stronger than any stone fortress.

options: He was a lost traveler from a distant foreign land.
